1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable three-player co-op dungeon crawler roguelite with at least seven classes, procedurally generated floors, escalating difficulty, and randomized three-option rewards after each floor.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone browser game in a single `index.html`, with canvas-rendered 2D gameplay and no external game engine.
- Supports local keyboard co-op and optional AI companions; touchscreen controls are included for mobile.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added eight selectable classes with individual stats and skills.
- Added procedurally generated connected dungeon rooms, enemies, and increasing floor difficulty.
- Added combat, enemy attacks, shared lives, class abilities, run tracking, and randomized three-choice floor rewards.
- Added responsive UI and mobile touch controls.
- Verified JavaScript syntax and launched a browser gameplay smoke test with no page errors.
- Captured and inspected `/tmp/opencode/game.jpg`.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

content.text:
Built the playable dungeon crawler in `index.html`. It includes eight selectable classes, three-player local controls with optional AI companions, procedurally generated floors with escalating enemy difficulty, class skills, shared lives, and a randomized choice of three party-wide rewards after each cleared floor.

Verified the game starts with three heroes and enemies, and the browser smoke test reported no page errors. Controls are shown in-game; on mobile, use the on-screen controls.
